messages:
Leah (product): Quick kickoff: enterprise pilot customers keep asking for an automated evidence pipeline for SOC2/ISO audits. Asks: signed tamper-evident audit exports, per-tenant retention lanes (including long-term cold), and a formal keystore/escrow proposal. We need to scope MVP for Dedicated and Private. Thoughts?
Tom (eng-plat): Agree. Proposed minimal deliverables: 1) self-service export portal (API + Console) that can package audit events + logs, 2) cryptographic signing of exports, 3) retention configuration per-tenant, 4) legal-hold override.
Sanjay (security): On signing: recommend using COSE (CBOR Object Signing and Encryption) for compact proofs and standard verification. Also propose a Merkle-root over the export blobs so customers can verify individual items without redownloading everything. Key management: support BYOK where tenant gives a public key (asymmetric) OR we do tenant-managed KMS integration (we call AsymmetricSign).
Ivy (ops): Search requirement: some customers need sub-5s query for incident investigations even over 2y of logs. We can't index 7y at that latency for everyone. Proposal: retention lanes: "Hot Index" (90d, sub-5s), "Warm Index" (2y, sub-30s), "Cold Archive" (7y, search within 24-72h). Expose cost opt-in per tenant.
Leah (product): Good. Also legal wants traceability on who requested exports and signed them. Add export audit events and proof-of-delivery (signed timestamped receipt).
Tom (eng-plat): Implementation sketch: export flow -> snapshot events -> compute Merkle tree -> package as tar.gz -> produce COSE_sign over {merkle_root, manifest, export_metadata, key_version} -> upload to customer bucket or provide signed URL. Include manifest with per-file sha256 and key metadata. Example manifest snippet:```json
{
  "format": "tar.gz",
  "files": [{"path":"audit/2026-03-01.log","sha256":"..."}],
  "merkle_root":"...",
  "signer":"projects/redwood-kms/keys/tenant1/versions/3"
}```
Sanjay (security): Rotation: store signer's key_version in manifest. When tenant rotates, we keep historic public keys (or allow tenants to publish archived public keys) so old exports verify. Consider publishing a time-stamped key registry (signed by our root) so tenants can fetch key history.
Ivy (ops): Operational concerns: export generation can be heavy CPU + egress. We should rate-limit exports and queue them. SLA asks from customers: "export ready within X hours". For pilot, suggest SLA: small exports < 24h, large (>100GB) best-effort. Also legal-hold must block scheduled purges.
Leah (product): Prioritization question: what must land in MVP vs future iterations? My suggestion: MVP = self-service export API + COSE signing + hot/warm/cold retention lanes + legal-hold + basic key rotation metadata. Future: Merkle partial proofs, time-stamped ledger, signed receipts, advanced search over cold archive.
Tom (eng-plat): Dev timeline estimate: 3 sprints for MVP features (export plumbing, signing integration, retention lanes), +1 sprint for export portal UI + RBAC. Merkle & ledger can be parallel spike.
Sanjay (security): Policy doc items: 1) threat model for export signing and key compromise, 2) rotation/escrow options (tenant escrow, third-party escrow, or our temporary escrow with HSM attestation), 3) verification UX in console. I'll draft policy.
Ivy (ops): Cost modeling: rough numbers: hot index ~ $0.025/GB/mo, warm ~ $0.008/GB/mo, cold archive object storage ~ $0.001/GB/mo + retrieval cost. Need to include CPU/export cost and egress in pricing appendix.
legal-bot: Legal note: include contract language for "evidence export availability" and a clause about retention overrides (legal-hold). We'll draft an SLA appendix. Tagging @legal to prepare template.
Leah (product): Action items: Tom prototype manifest+COSE sample by EOD Friday, Sanjay to post rotation/escrow options doc by Tue, Ivy to produce cost model and suggested tenant opt-in tiers, legal to draft SLA appendix. I’ll synthesize a short PRD and host a 30m scoping meeting.
Tom (eng-plat): Will post prototype and a tiny CLI example: `redwood export create --tenant t123 --since 2026-01-01 --signed=COSE`
Sanjay (security): I'll include verification checklist: "fetch public key -> verify COSE signature -> verify merkle root -> spot-check file hashes".
Ivy (ops): I'll enumerate operational guards: concurrent export caps, max export size, dry-run option.
Leah (product): Great. Thanks everyone :rocket: Meeting invite in 10m for follow-up.
